He played college basketball for [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]]. ==High school career== Caupain attended [[Cosby High School]] and started on the basketball team as a sophomore, averaging 7 points per game. Moving to point guard, he scored 25.7 points per game and was named All-Metro as a junior. As a senior, he scored 26 points and pulled down 15.1 rebounds per game. Caupain was named All-Metro player of the year.{{cite news|last1=Kolenich|first1=Eric|title=Caupain is boys basketball player of the year|url=http://www.richmond.com/sports/high-school/honors/caupain-is-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/article_0b026b58-999d-11e2-8c93-0019bb30f31a.html|accessdate=June 27, 2017|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|date=March 31, 2013}} ==College career== In Caupain's freshman season at Cincinnati, he served as a backup to star [[Sean Kilpatrick]] and participated in the team's asphyxiating defense.{{cite magazine|last1=Hamilton|first1=Brian|title=Cincinnati, finally on the offensive, looks primed for long stay in NCAAs|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/02/13/cincinnati-bearcats-offense-troy-caupain-mick-cronin|accessdate=June 27, 2017|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=February 14, 2017}} As a sophomore, Caupain averaged 9.4 points and 3.6 assists per game. He was named Honorable Mention All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]].{{cite web|title=2015 American Athletic Conference All-Conference Teams|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2015/3/10/MBB_0310150708.aspx|website=theAmerican.org|date=March 10, 2015 |publisher=Sidearmsports|accessdate=June 27, 2017}} As a junior, he was named to the First Team All-AAC.{{cite web|title=American Men's Basketball All-Conference and All-Rookie Teams Announced|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2016/3/7/MBB_0307164437.aspx|website=American Athletic Conference|date=March 8, 2016 |publisher=Sidearm Sports|accessdate=June 27, 2017}} Caupain led the team in scoring and assists with 13.0 points and 4.8 assists per game while contributing to a 22–11 season.{{cite news|last1=Groeschen|first1=Tom|title=UC basketball: 'Huge expectations'|url=http://www.newarkadvocate.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2016/10/06/uc-basketball-huge-expectations/91679266/|accessdate=June 27, 2017|work=[[The Newark Advocate]]|date=October 6, 2016}} [[File:Troy Caupain.jpg|thumb|left|Caupain with Cincinnati in December 2016]] Coming into his senior year, Cincinnati was picked to win the AAC regular season title and Caupain was voted as AAC Preseason Co-Player of the Year.{{cite press release|title=Cincinnati Voted as 2016–17 American Men's Basketball Favorite|date=October 24, 2016|publisher=American Athletic|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2016/10/20/MBB_1020162600.aspx|accessdate=October 24, 2016}} He averaged 10.5 points, 4.6 rebounds and 4.4 assists in 2016–17, finishing sixth in Division 1 with a 3.36-to-1 assist to turnover ratio. Caupain was named first team NABC All-District 25 and Second Team All-AAC.{{cite news|title=Brimah, Caupain, Moore, Williams Join NBA Squads|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2017/6/23/MBB_0623172329.aspx?path=mbball|accessdate=June 27, 2017|work=[[American Athletic Conference]]|date=June 26, 2017}} He helped lead the Bearcats to a 30–6 record and the university's seventh consecutive NCAA Tournament appearance. In his career, he had a school-record 515 assists and scored 1,317 points, tying [[Cashmere Wright]] for 22nd place on the school all-time scoring list.{{cite news|last1=Groeschen|first1=Tom|title=UC's Caupain to get chance with NBA team|url=http://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2017/06/24/ucs-caupain-get-chance-nba-team/426126001/|accessdate=June 27, 2017|work=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]]|date=June 24, 2017}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2017 NBA draft]], Caupain signed a summer league contract with the NBA's [[Toronto Raptors]] and received a subsequent training camp invite from the [[Orlando Magic]] on August 31,{{cite news|title=Magic Sign Troy Caupain and Kalin Lucas|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-troy-caupain-and-kalin-lucas|accessdate=April 15, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=August 31, 2017}} however, he was waived on October 13.{{cite news|title=Magic Waive Troy Caupain and Rodney Purvis|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-troy-caupain-and-rodney-purvis|accessdate=April 15, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2017}} Ten days later, he was acquired by the [[Lakeland Magic]] of the [[NBA G League]],{{cite news|first=Ashley|last=Foss|title=Lakeland Magic announces 2017–18 training camp roster|url=https://lakeland.gleague.nba.com/news/lakeland-magic-announces-2017-18-training-camp-roster/|accessdate=April 15, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2017}} averaging 15.8 points, 7.5 rebounds, 5.7 assists and 1.4 steals in 51 games.{{cite news|title=GSA Udine signs Troy Caupain|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/Italy/news/528706/GSA-Udine-signs-Troy-Caupain|accessdate=April 15, 2018|work=Eurobasket.com|date=April 4, 2018}} On April 4, 2018, after the conclusion of the G League season, Caupain signed with [[APU Udine|G.S.A. Udine]] of the Italian [[Serie A2 Basket]]. On July 11, 2018, Caupain signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Orlando Magic. Under the terms of the deal, Caupain split time with Orlando and their NBA G League affiliate, the Lakeland Magic.{{cite web|title=Magic Sign Troy Caupain to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-troy-caupain-two-way-contract |accessdate=July 11, 2018 |website=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 11, 2018}} Caupain made his NBA debut on December 31, 2018, in a 125–100 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]], scoring five points with two assists in five minutes of playing time.{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandopinstripedpost.com/2018/12/31/18163321/orlando-magic-charlotte-hornets-recap|title=Hornets 125, Magic 100: Shorthanded Magic end 2018 with ugly loss|first=Mike|last=Cali|work=OrlandoPinstripedPost.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=December 31, 2018|access-date=January 2, 2018}} On September 12, 2019, Caupain joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for training camp.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Three Players Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2019/9/12/blazers-announce-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|accessdate=September 13, 2019|date=September 12, 2019}} On October 18, 2019, the Trail Blazers waived Caupain.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Waive Blevins Caupain and Perrantes|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2019/10/18/blazers-waive-blevins-caupain-perrantes|website=NBA.com|accessdate=November 4, 2019|date=October 18, 2019}} On November 3, 2019, Caupain
